name: Lazarus Shelf Street Clinic RipDoc Full Rig
description: A full-length butcher-gray apron over salvaged olive scrubs, both stained with chromatic fluid and sealed with peel-strip biohazard patches. Cracked visor headset holds three mismatched magnification lenses taped into a single rig. Knee-high rubber overboots seal over the scrubs, and nitrile-coated gauntlets extend past the wrist with grip-textured fingertips. A chest harness of repurposed cargo webbing holds scalpel rolls, syringe loops, and a portable neural-clamp bracket.
functionality: Fluid-resistant apron and sealed overboots protect against blood and coolant splash; tool harness keeps surgical implements within one-handed reach during solo procedures.
what_it_says: This person has kept people alive in conditions that would shut down a licensed clinic, and they've done it without asking for credentials.
story_hooks: A fresh neural port on the apron's shoulder strap suggests the doc recently performed self-surgery — the sutures are still visible.
The cracked visor has a hand-scratched serial number that matches a stolen Lazarus MedCore diagnostic unit reported missing six months ago.

Novafold Pharmaceuticals GraftSkin TS-7 Bioprinted Dermal Replacement Sheet

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian, improvisational medical rig that reads as street-level emergency medicine—survival-focused rather than sterile. The silhouette is bulky and intentionally over-armored, layering protection over function. This is the uniform of someone who patches people in ungoverned zones where proper facilities don't exist.
physical_description.fit: Deliberately oversized and loose-fitting to accommodate movement, augmentation ports, and layered protection. The apron drapes heavily; the scrubs underneath are relaxed. Gauntlets are snug at the wrist but flare slightly over the forearm. Overboots are stiff and deliberate, not tailored.
physical_description.primary_material: Butcher-gray canvas apron (food-grade industrial salvage); olive cotton-poly blend scrubs (surplus military or corporate medical); cracked polymer visor; nitrile-coated nylon gauntlets; vulcanized rubber overboots; repurposed mil-spec cargo webbing chest harness
physical_description.texture: Rough, worn canvas; stiff scrub fabric softened by repeated use; cracked visor plastic with visible hairline fractures; tacky nitrile coating on gauntlets; deeply treaded rubber soles; frayed webbing edges
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant butcher-gray apron, olive drab scrubs underneath, gunmetal gray visor, black nitrile gauntlets and overboots, tan and forest-green webbing harness. Chromatic fluid stains (iridescent cyan, biohazard yellow, blood-rust) create accidental pattern across torso.
physical_description.closures: Apron ties with reinforced stitching; scrubs have friction-fit drawstring waist; visor headset friction-locked with taped magnification lenses; gauntlets secured with elastic cuff bands; overboots zip or friction-fit; harness buckles are salvaged mil-spec (worn brass).
distinctive_features: Three mismatched magnification lenses jury-rigged onto a single cracked visor—taped, not welded
Peel-strip biohazard patches covering older stains (layered history of use)
Chest harness with purpose-built tool loops: scalpel roll pockets, syringe retention loops, bracketed mount for portable neural-clamp
Grip-textured nitrile fingertips on gauntlets (tactile precision despite heavy protection)
Knee-high rubber overboots designed to seal against biological hazards
Visible wear, fraying at seams, scuffs on visor, repaired patches on apron
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 / Tier 4 borderline. This is sub-grade or working-class street medical. The components are salvaged, improvised, or surplus—no new-manufacture luxury marks. Worn openly as a badge of ungoverned medicine.
physical_description.cultural_context: Street doc, RipDoc, black-market surgeon, or emergency clinic operator in Tier 5 autonomous zones. Wearing this signals practical competence without oversight, willingness to operate where corpo medicine won't go, and acceptance of biohazard exposure. This is the uniform of survival medicine.
physical_description.condition_typical: Heavily used, stained, patched, and worn. The visor is cracked; the fabric shows chemical burns and chromatic fluid residue. Everything is functional but visibly exhausted—maintenance through repair, not replacement.
